        "Historical discovery starts four ordinary sources in intentional priority order (fromDisk, fromISP, fromDB, forMX), plus separate Exchange discovery.         "Current whole269-line module has evolved to an async generator. Ordinary sources share external/internal abort signals and promiseFirstSuccessful waits in priority order, then aborts lower-priority work; Exchange receives only the external signal. These later accepted semantics are current context, not retroactively attributed to the original fatal401 behavior.",
        "Current email #findConfig forwards generator feedback, distinguishes an actionable credential error, checks the aborted signal, falls back to guessing, fills discovered config and calls ewsifyConfig. #handleAbortable aborts first, then resumes a paused stream with acceptRedirect:false, catches rejection and clears it. Current unit tasks cover success/missing, HTTPS auth/password/separate username, redirect refusal/acceptance, valid ordinary config despite401 and abort-before-first-next. They do not exercise every in-flight wizard cancellation race. Actual build registration and TOML test manifest were read; former INI absence is scoped proof.",
        "Current ewsifyConfig clones the Exchange incoming object, sets type:ews and useGlobalPreferredServer:false, then appends or replaces it according to add-on coexistence. The historical OAuth code appends an EWS scope before destructuring provider values over it; that sequence is no longer in the accepted function. Current EWS test actually checks the old supplied OWA URL, despite its message saying EWS.AccessAsUser.All. The message does not prove an EWS scope was added. No new policy or runtime permission result is inferred.",
        "D225130 full creation-to-backout/reland timeline and every actual submitted historical inline were read.
